To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a new approach of implementing fault tolerance for COTS devices that (1) does not require any adaptation of the software and (2) does not require the use of expensive dedicated fault tolerant hardware.

(1) the proposed architecture allows to implement transparent replication of software components without the necessity to adapt the functional program, (2) the proposed architecture enables a flexible and cheap way to implement fault tolerance in hardware, and (3) the proposed architecture is applicable to a broad range of safety-critical applications

(1) transparent replication of software is possible leveraging modern SoC features, (2) this replication is transparent to the application and (3) the performance of the presented approach is comparable to the performance of commonly deployed software based fault tolerant approaches
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for transparent replication and hardware monitoring of safety critical software using chip built in mechanisms of modern COTS devices.
the development of fault tolerant board architectures based on COTS components, which are capable to tolerate hardware and software faults.
the question, how to build fault-tolerant architectures using modern COTS SoCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is a very promising and innovative way to build fault tolerant board architectures for COTS components.
the described approach is feasible and has a significant potential to improve the state of the art of fault tolerance in safety critical systems.
the presented approach is a viable option to build fault tolerant systems out of modern COTS components and to separate functional and fault tolerant code.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented approach allows to build fault tolerant systems relatively cheaply out COTS components and to include legacy code in fault tolerance architectures without the need of any adaptation.
the described approach is a promising solution for building fault tolerant architectures out of modern COTS SoC devices.

we were able to implement transparent software replication on a COTS SoC platform without the need of software adaptation and with a significant performance gain compared to commonly deployed software replication approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
modern COTS devices can be utilized to build fault tolerant systems with a relatively high degree of transparency for the application software.
the presented approach allows to build fault tolerant hardware architectures out of COTS devices relatively cheaply and without the need to modify the application software.
modern SoCs provide sufficient hardware features to implement replication of software components transparent to the application software and without the need for software adaptation.
